title: Default-on assistant in a workplace chat and meetings app
question: What could happen if Microsoft integrates Copilot more deeply into Teams and enables additional AI capabilities by default?

quote.text: Tenant administrators decide which features are on, and any change goes through a two-week review by the security team and the records manager.

participants.name: Security reviewers

quote.text: The security reviewers read the assistant's documentation as saying that it respects each person's existing permissions, and they do not dispute that.

participants.rationale: Review every change before it goes live.

participants.name: Records manager

quote.text: The records manager asked how long they are kept, whether they fall under legal hold and whether an employee can delete a recap about themselves.

participants.rationale: Co-reviews every change and owns retention.

participants.name: Helpdesk

quote.text: The helpdesk lead expects more questions from ordinary users about the new panel and wants a short guide ready on day one.

participants.rationale: Absorbs the questions after a change.

participants.name: Ordinary users

quote.text: The helpdesk lead expects more questions from ordinary users about the new panel and wants a short guide ready on day one.

participants.rationale: Employees who see the new panel and the recaps.

participants.name: Client-facing department managers

quote.text: Department managers in client-facing teams like the idea of recaps but are uneasy about clients receiving automatic summaries of calls.

participants.rationale: Like recaps but worry about clients receiving them.

quote.text: Employee representatives have asked whether recaps could end up in performance reviews.
The finance team asked whether features that arrive by default would be charged to the firm, and nobody has been able to answer.
Two of the firm's larger clients have their own rules on recording and transcription.

participants.name: Managed-service partner

quote.text: The managed-service partner that supports the tenant bills by the hour for configuration work.

participants.rationale: Supports the tenant and bills for configuration.

participants.name: Rival collaboration suite vendors

quote.text: Some staff work inside a client's tenant on a rival collaboration suite, and a few power users have tried that suite's assistant on the side.

participants.rationale: Offer assistants that users already try.

quote.text: The data protection officer expects that regulators in some regions would ask how employees are told about AI processing of meetings.

participants.name: Internal auditors

quote.text: Internal auditors asked for a log of when recaps were generated, and the tenant report gives daily counts, not counts per meeting.

participants.rationale: Ask for a log the tenant report does not give.

participants.name: Frontline and shift workers

quote.text: No frontline or shift workers were in the group.

participants.rationale: Named only as absent from the pilot.

participants.name: External guests in meetings

quote.text: There is no record of how external guests reacted to automatic recaps.

participants.rationale: Named only as a group nobody has heard from.

constraints.quote: Tenant administrators decide which features are on, and any change goes through a two-week review by the security team and the records manager.
constraints.rationale: A mandatory review before any change.

constraints.quote: Two of the firm's larger clients have their own rules on recording and transcription.
constraints.rationale: Client rules bind the firm's work for them.

constraints.quote: Clients in some countries need consent before a meeting is transcribed.
The review board meets in three weeks.
constraints.rationale: A date the decision is tied to.

constraints.quote: No licence terms for newly default-on features are in hand, so the finance team cannot say who pays or whether people without a licence would see anything.
Administrators ask for a separate switch for each new feature and enough notice to test it.
constraints.rationale: A request about how a change should be rolled out.

constraints.quote: The retention schedule has no entry for AI-generated summaries.
Internal auditors asked for a log of when recaps were generated, and the tenant report gives daily counts, not counts per meeting.
constraints.rationale: The report cannot show what auditors want.

gap.removeText: Clients in some countries need consent before a meeting is transcribed.
gap.rationale: The only statement that consent is needed.

alternatives.rationale: Administrators ask for a staged rollout.

claims.statement: Weekly use of the meeting recap feature reached 41% of pilot seats at the end of the pilot.
The review board meets in three weeks.
Most administrators said they would turn off new assistant features by default until a review was finished.
claims.rationale: 44% said so; that is not most.

claims.statement: The pilot measured the time saved by recaps independently.
claims.rationale: The source says it was not measured independently.

claims.statement: Frontline and shift workers rated the recap feature highly in the pilot.
claims.rationale: No frontline workers were in the pilot.

claims.statement: Self-reported time saved had a median of 25 minutes a week.

a.quote: Weekly use of the meeting recap feature reached 41% of pilot seats at the end of the pilot.

b.quote: weekly use of the meeting recap feature reached 68% of seats in its early-adopter tenants

conflicts.rationale: Two weekly-use figures for the same feature that disagree; the populations differ, which a reader must weigh.
